headline: Still spending, but choosy: value wins, housing stalls, the affluent hold up
summary: Sales are still growing at almost every big retailer and most beat profit estimates, but shoppers are trading down, traffic is moving to the cheapest formats, and housing-linked spending is flat. One-time tariff refunds flattered many of the profit beats.
implications: Consumption is slowing, not contracting: median comps near +3.7%, driven by more shoppers at value chains rather than bigger baskets.
Lower- and middle-income budgets are stretched by fuel and food; higher earners keep spending, trading down at discounters while still buying luxury at full price.
Goods prices should ease: retailers say they are passing tariff refunds through as price cuts.

segments.mass: Traffic up at Walmart, Costco and Target; Walmart U.S. comps slowed to +2.6% as fuel squeezed budgets.
segments.ecom: Amazon's +2% is a Prime Day timing quirk; eBay (+16%) and Etsy (+8.8%) sped up and raised outlooks.
segments.home: Flat: Home Depot +1.3%, Lowe's +0.2%, fewer transactions; big remodels wait for housing turnover.
segments.offprice: Strongest segment: Ross +10% on traffic; TJX +4%, with HomeGoods +7%.
segments.value: Traffic-led gains (+3.5% to +3.7%) as higher earners trade in; core low-income shoppers still stretched.
segments.electronics: Best Buy +4.5% on PC replacement and new gadgets: fewer, pricier items.
segments.luxury: Split: Coach and Ralph Lauren sell at full price (North America +4% and +6%) and LVMH U.S. +5%, but Michael Kors Americas fell 11%.
segments.grocery: Kroger barely growing (+0.2%) on drug-price rules and cautious shoppers; sales outlook cut.
